**Additional Questions** can be included to assess higher-level thinking skills.

- **LED Knowledge Check:** students can use the LEDs to build a conditional statement

e. Cross-Curricular Connections

- The International Collegiate Inventors Competition has students create prototypes based on the material libraries around them from the previous class. This provides students with grades against it.
- Could also address engagement for middle school/ high school students.

**Mentoring Plan**

- Experience levels with the lab provided is a valuable addition for students at the high school/ college levels.
- Another consideration would be collecting materials from the lab and going through the simulation on the Nanomole board.
- Students would have the ability to analyze the code in order to refine the simulation of their devices.
- Students will be able to practice social-emotional learning skills by discussing with their peers
- Think/Pair-Share can be used to assess higher level thinking skills
-  Small group discussion
- Competition could be a motivator for students

**Scenario**

- The students are asked to answer the following scenario: Using the gripper slider Hi on the IRT3X9013 and design a gripper to hold a box up to his shoulder. The gripper should be able to hold up to 10 lb. The gripper must use a servo motor to do so.

**Readout Sensors**

- The lab included readout instrs on the labaxis.
- Students could use the labaxis for insight into how much force was applied by the gripper to hold the box. They could then plot physical data for readout instruments to correlate with simulation results.
- Compare those results to the data before simulating booths for the "different selection" category we discussed should they get similar results.
- Students will need to establish if this is a 1:1 or > 1:1 case.
- Their readout should be relative to the displacement zero point and not absolute. The induction travel can be a target for learning more about their readout capabilities.

**Bench Projects**

- Students could design a robot that hooks a car tire with motor and communicates with the command it receives.
- Students will need to realize an enclosure for the robot to contain the motor so that it does not drift away, then they will need to simulate this in Geogebra then translate that simulation into Labaxis.

**Additional Thinking Scales**

- **Causal Thinking** - "What would happen if we changed variables in this lab to see what happens?"
- **Action Plan** - "What would happen if we built a device that does this?"
- **Process Evaluation** - "How well did our device work?"
- **Self-Awareness** - "What do we know about robotics and how to safely operate industrial robots?"

emitting element.The figure contains two subfigures. 

**Subfigure 1:**

- **Title:** Fig. 9. Maximum Drain Current Vs. Case Temperature.
- **Description:**
  - This graph shows how the drain current, measured in units of \(I_{\text{D}}\), varies with temperature (\(T_{\text{C}}\)) and Case Temperature for a Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (MOSFET).
  - The x-axis represents the case temperature, while the y-axis represents the drain current.
  - Different curves are plotted for varying temperature:
    - Dark blue: Case temperature within the range \(25 - 175^\circ \text{C}\).
    - Red: \(T_{\text{C}} = 0.5 \text{ V}\).
    - Dark grey: \(T = 1 \text{ V}\).
    - Light grey: \(T = 2 \text{ V}\).
    - Dark yellow: \(T = 5 \text{ V}\).
    - Dark blue (line with triangles): \(T = 10 \text{ V}\).
    - Dark blue (line with circles): \(T = 30 \text{ V}\).
- The vertical dashed lines denote the temperatures at which the measurement's receiver antenna is closed for each respective operating voltage.

**Subfigure 2:**

- **Title:** Fig. 10a. Switching Time Test Circuit.
- **Description:**
  - This diagram illustrates the test circuit schematic involved in measuring the switching time.
  - The key elements include:
    - **V\({}_{\text{DS}}\):** Drain-source voltage applied.
    - **V\({}_{\text{GS}}\):** Gate-source voltage applied for controlling the MOSFET.
    - **V\({}_{\text{DD}}\):** Voltage related to case temperature (\(T_{\text{C}}\)).
    - **DUT:** Device under test, presumably the MOSFET.
    - **\(R_{\text{D}}\):** DIBL device resistance.
- **Legend:**
  - \(t_{\text{t}}\) represents the duration of the pulse in seconds.
  - \(V_{\text{DD}}\) is set to increase in steps, ensuring the gate-source voltage never falls below V\({}_{\text{DD}}\).
  - \(R_{\text{D}}\) is the total resistor value of \(R_{\text{D}} + R_{\text{off}}\) where \(R_{\text{off}}\) is defined in the text.

**Subfigure 3:**

- **Title:** Fig. 10b. Switching Time Waveforms.
- **Description:**
  - This plot shows the voltage response of the device under test during switching time for two different values of \(V_{\text{DS}}\) (left y-axis, dark blue: \(V_{\text{DS}} = 0.5 V\) and right y-axis, dark blue: \(V_{\text{DS}} = 5 V\)).
  - The x-axis is Time, and the y-axis is the output voltage response.
  - Two cases are represented:
    - **Case 1:**
      - Pulse width is 1 \(\mu \text{s}\).
      - DUT characteristics are : \(R_{\text{D}} = 100k \Omega\), load resistance \(R = 1 k \Omega\).
      - Constant voltage at \(V_{\text{DD}} = 2 V\).
    - **Case 2:**
      - DUT characteristics have \(R_{\text{D}} = 1 k \Omega\).
      - Other variables maintain the same settings as in Case 1.
  - For Case 2, the pulse width is 10 \(\mu \text{s}\), the pulse duration is 1 \(\mu \text{s}\), and the amplitude of the control voltage is \(V_{\text{GS}} = 5 V\).
  - Indicate  rout that the reflected channel value \(Y^\text{RC}\) (in V) influences the case on the right of the graph after switching and defines the case signal.

This figure collectively illustrates the investigation of the drain current and the switching characteristics of a MOSFET based on various environmental conditions and device parameters.
